newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch oil and gas sector set for mini-boom in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch oil and gas sector set for mini-boom in 1997.

text.p: Growth in activity and investment will lead to a minor renaissance in the mature Dutch oil and gas sector next year, official data released this week showed.
The Dutch Central Bureau of Statistics said it believed investment in oil and coal processing, principally oil refining, had risen by 64 percent in 1996 from 700 million guilders in 1995.
But in 1997 it expected investment to more than triple. Overall, manufacturing investment was expected to rise by 22 percent in 1997.
In the oil refining sector, both Shell and Nerefco are to upgrade their refineries in Rotterdam.

Shell is nearing the end of its 3.2 billion guilder "PER+" project, a scheme involving the construction of a new hydrocracker at their Pernis site near Rotterdam, in addition to a gas production plant and two cogeneration units.
Most of the investment, however, is now over and the plant is due to be completed by the end of May.

Further down the Maas river, the BP/Texaco joint venture Nerefco is to plough 350 million guilders into its Europoort refinery until 1998 with construction of a desulphurisation plant and renovation of a crude distillation unit.
But Nerefco's other Rotterdam refinery, at Pernis, is due to close in 1999.

Investment in renovation and construction of power stations will also be at a high of 500 million guilders in 1997, according to the power generating body Sep. Investment is projected to fall below 350 million per year in the following four years.

In mining and quarrying, dominated by oil and gas exploration, investment dipped by 1.8 percent this year from 1.8 billion guilders, but the CBS expects a 46 percent improvement in investment in 1997.

Last month, Edinburgh-based industry analysts Wood Mackenzie said that exploration companies had begun targeting Dutch satellite gas fields. The increased activity and improving success rate would lead to a peak of capital expenditure of 2.2 billion guilders in 1997.

In October, Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM), a 50/50 joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon, said it had made a "promising" gas discovery in the Wadden Sea, part of the North Sea off the north coast of the Netherlands.
A spokesman for Gasunie, the Dutch monopoly supplier, said the find was likely to amount to at least 200 billion cubic metres.
Next year, Amoco Netherlands will complete the 300 million guilder construction of emergency gas stores. Construction began last year.
Gasunie's larger Langelo storage site will also be completed by the end of 1997.

Most significantly, work should also begin on compressing the Netherlands' largest gas field. In November, NAM awarded a one billion guilder contract to a consortium led by Dutch industrial group Stork to compress and renovate the Slochteren gas field in the northern province of Groningen.
The growth of manufacturing investment in the oil sector is particularly needed in an area suffering some structural decline.

Economic growth in the Rotterdam area still lags behind other parts of the country. The situation was particularly bleak for the region's extensive petrochemicals industry, according to a study published on Wednesday by the Rotterdam Chamber of Commerce.
The study said the sector's revenue actually declined in 1996. However, the number of job vacancies rose to a level unmatched since 1992 and business confidence also picked up.
